decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach with the left arm toward the left tube; right arm stays at origin.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller increments, pitching the left gripper down while approaching the left tube.
Align open jaws over the left tube, using its visible long axis; finish the slow top-down approach before grasping.
Make a small wrist-view centering correction, lower to grasp height, and close around the first tube.
Lift the closed left gripper with a slight retreat, checking that the first tube follows before transfer.
The first tube remains between the jaws; start rotating it upright while moving toward the left rack slot.
Continue the controlled upright rotation and transfer above the rack, keeping the tube closed in the left gripper.
Finish making the held tube vertical and pause above the leftmost large slot to assess alignment before insertion.
Apply a small lateral alignment correction and lower the vertical tube toward the selected rack opening, retaining the grasp.
Lower the first tube slowly to insertion depth while keeping it vertical and the gripper closed.
The tube appears to have met the front rim rather than seated. Lift to clear it and correct alignment farther into the rack before retrying.
Retry a slow vertical insertion at the corrected rack alignment, watching for further slipping or rim contact.
Complete a shallow final insertion and release the first tube, allowing it to settle into the opening before withdrawing.
Withdraw the open left gripper from the seated tube while starting an elbow-up right-arm approach to the nearer right tube.
The released tube is upright in the rack. Return the left arm toward origin and continue pitching the right gripper over the next tube.
Bring the right jaws into a top-down alignment over the nearer tube while completing the left-arm return.
Center the right gripper using the wrist view, descend the last centimeters, and close on the second tube.
Lift the second tube with the right gripper closed and a small retreat, checking retention before rotation toward the rack.
Rotate the retained second tube upright while transferring toward the middle rack slot, with the left arm parked clear.
Continue the smooth right-arm rotation and transfer above the middle slot, keeping the second tube securely closed.
Finish bringing the second tube vertical over the middle opening; keep clearance above the rack for visual alignment.
Center the upright second tube slightly left and descend toward the middle slot, maintaining a closed gripper.
Lower the second tube vertically into the middle opening, stopping at insertion height to verify seating before release.
Release the second tube in the middle slot, then withdraw the open right gripper slightly to verify that it stands independently.
Both released tubes appear upright in separate slots. Move the open right gripper up and away from the rack toward the remaining far-right tube.
Begin a raised elbow-up arc toward the last tube, rotating the right wrist toward its diagonal long axis.
Continue the open-gripper approach toward the remaining tube, keeping the elbow-up configuration and lowering gradually.
Finish the top-down approach above the last tube and inspect the wrist view before making the grasp-height descent.
Refine the last tube's diagonal alignment and move the open jaws toward its body while descending slowly.
Make the final small body-centering adjustment, descend to grasp height, and close the right gripper on the last tube.
Lift the last tube clear of the table with the right gripper closed, retreating slightly to preserve elbow-up reach margin.
The last tube follows the gripper. Begin rotating it upright and transferring inward toward the unoccupied right rack slot.
Continue the raised transfer and upright rotation of the last tube, keeping clear of the two inserted tubes.
Finish the upright rotation above the unoccupied right slot, maintaining a closed grasp and clearance from the inserted tubes.
Refine lateral alignment over the right opening and lower the last tube toward the rack, keeping it upright and closed.
Lower the last tube vertically into the right slot to insertion height; hold closed until seating is checked.
The last tube appears to have contacted the front rim and slipped upward. Lift clear and shift slightly farther into the rack before retrying.
Retry a slow vertical insertion at the corrected right-slot alignment, checking whether the tube passes the rim without further slipping.
Finish a shallow insertion and open the gripper so the last tube can settle; begin a small withdrawal to check independent seating.
Withdraw clear of the released last tube and let it settle, inspecting whether it becomes upright and reaches the same depth as the others.
The last tube has tipped out rather than seated. Move the open gripper clear for a better view before a recovery grasp.
Raise the open right gripper clear of the fallen tube and allow it to settle before planning a fresh grasp.
Approach the settled tube for recovery, rotating the open right wrist to match its new diagonal axis.
Continue the recovery approach with open jaws, slowly rotating downward while keeping the elbow-up posture.
Align the recovery grasp with the settled tube's long axis and bring the open jaws directly above its body.
Descend onto the recovered tube with a small centering correction and close around the body rather than the cap.
Lift the recovered tube with the right gripper closed, checking retention before another controlled rack approach.
The recovered tube remains held. Begin a slow upright rotation toward the free right slot, preserving clearance and configuration continuity.
Continue the recovered tube's upright rotation and slow transfer above the right slot, keeping the grasp closed.
Bring the recovered tube fully vertical above the free opening, then assess its tip alignment before descending.
Lower the recovered upright tube toward the right opening with a small lateral correction, retaining the grasp for a closer alignment check.
